newsitem.title: INDIA: Mandela says Zaire peace efforts under U.N. role.
newsitem.headline: Mandela says Zaire peace efforts under U.N. role.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela said on Friday that his country's role in hosting peace talks expected next week between Zairean rebels and representatives of President Mobutu Sese Seko should be counted within peace initiatives led by the United Nations.

"It is in that context that the role of South Africa should be assessed," he told a news conference in New Delhi. "We must not exaggerate the role played by South Africa in that country," said Mandela, who was on a three-day visit to India.

Mandela, responding to a question on South Africa's hosting of the talks, implicitly confirmed a South African government source who said earlier on Friday in Johannesburg that the two sides in the central African nation were scheduled to meet in South Africa.
The source told Reuters that senior foreign ministry officials had started laying the groundwork for negotiations, which were likely to take place on Monday or Tuesday.
Earlier on Friday Zairean rebels said talks would take place in South Africa on Monday or Tuesday.

Forces led by the rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (AFDL) under leader Laurent Kabila have seized about a quarter of Africa's third largest country and insist that a ceasefire in the six month civil war can only be declared after negotiations have begun.
